stage1_evidence_shown.label: OBJECTIVE
stage1_evidence_shown.context: To characterize the use and delivery of cough and cold medicines in children younger than 6 presenting to an inner-city pediatric emergency department (PED) following 2007 FDA warnings.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: A cross-sectional observational study was performed using a convenience sampling of PED patients during the fall of 2010. Caregivers were presented with 6 commonly used cough medicine preparations and were asked to demonstrate if and how they would administer these to their children.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: In all, 65 patients and their caregivers consented and participated in the study. During the demonstration, 82% (53/65) stated that they would treat with cough or cold medicines, and 72% (38/53) incorrectly dosed the medication they desired to give.
